key_insight: A multi-domain EEG model that combines spectral, connectivity, and topological features improved subject-level ADHD classification, with SVM performing best.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support more objective, non-invasive ADHD biomarker research by capturing brain-signal patterns that single-feature models may miss.
method: EEG from 121 subjects was preprocessed and split into overlapping windows.
Features were extracted from three domains: spectral measures, wPLI-based functional connectivity, and persistent homology/topology descriptors.
Recursive Feature Elimination reduced 1,043 features to 110, and five classifiers were tested with stratified five-fold cross-validation.
evidence_signal: In cross-validated evaluation, SVM achieved 80.17% accuracy, 80.95% F1-score, 80.14% balanced accuracy, 86.72% ROC-AUC, and 87.34% PR-AUC.
watch_item: Results come from a relatively small cohort and window-based feature aggregation, so external validation on independent datasets is needed before broader use.
paper_title: A Multi-Domain EEG Framework Integrating Spectral, Functional Connectivity, and Topological Features for Subject-Level ADHD Classification
